response.passage: In geometry, an angle is formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint called the vertex. The size of an angle depends entirely on the amount of rotation between its two arms, not on the physical length of those arms. If you extend the arms of an angle, the angle measurement remains unchanged. A straight angle measures exactly 180 degrees and is considered a valid angle, even though it appears as a straight line. When using a protractor, you must place the centre mark exactly on the vertex and align the baseline with one arm to get an accurate reading. Regarding shapes, a triangle is classified as isosceles if at least two of its sides are equal in length, regardless of the length of the third side. Furthermore, all squares are special types of rectangles because they possess four right angles and opposite sides that are parallel. When identifying 3D solids, remember that edges are the straight line segments where two faces meet, and curved boundaries are not considered edges. For example, a cylinder has two circular faces and one curved surface, but it has zero straight edges. Always focus on the properties of the shape rather than its orientation or size to classify it correctly.
response.summary: Angles are defined by rotation, not arm length, and straight lines can be 180-degree angles. Shapes like squares and isosceles triangles are classified by their properties, not their appearance or orientation. Edges in 3D geometry refer strictly to straight lines where faces meet.
